key_insight: At 12.5% La substitution in BaTiO₃, enhanced electronic screening is linked to weaker ferroelectric polarization, lower static dielectric response, and reduced optical anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Donor substitution offers a design lever for balancing polarization, dielectric response, and near-edge optical transparency in perovskite oxides.
method: Density functional theory for structure, energetics, and electronic and optical properties
Density-functional perturbation theory for phonons, dielectric response, and Born effective charges
evidence_signal: Calculations show reduced tetragonality and Ti off-centering, polar-mode hardening, smaller anomalous Born effective charges, and an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein–Moss-type mechanism.
watch_item: Results apply to the modeled 12.5% La composition; additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.
paper_title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
